chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, for Paradise there is a gate called Al-Maʿrūf (Kindness/Goodness). None shall enter it except the people of Al-Maʿrūf. And the people of Al-Maʿrūf in the world are the people of Al-Maʿrūf in the Hereafter.

key_terms.الْمَعْرُوفُ: Kindness, goodness, or recognized virtuous acts

ai.seo_question: What is the gate of Paradise called for those who perform acts of kindness?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), establishing 'Al-Maʿrūf' not merely as a general virtue but as a specific spiritual gate to Paradise, highlighting the continuity between worldly conduct and eternal reward. This narration underscores the Shia concept of *al-Maʿrūf* as a defining characteristic of the faithful, linking their social reputation for kindness directly to their eschatological recognition. It serves as a practical reminder that consistent, visible goodness in this life is the prerequisite for entry through this specific gate.
